146198.why:
What I did: the word this case tells you to type, ZZLONGROW, sits at the START of the name, where a cut from the right can never reach it — so typing it makes this case pass no matter how badly the row is cut. This case’s own BEFORE YOU START asks for a match near the END of the value, so I typed Fernvale, which sits in the part of these same records that gets cut off. The Expected Results were not changed.
What I saw: work orders S2-34379 and S2-34376 come back, and the word Fernvale is nowhere on either row. The cut removes it completely. The row comes back and cannot say why.
How I know the search panel can show it: two other rows in the very same list, S2-34360 and S2-34157, do show Fernvale highlighted. So these two rows are genuinely hiding it.
Also worth fixing in this case itself: the word it tells the tester to type cannot show the problem it is looking for. A change to BEFORE YOU START is proposed separately.

146209.why:
This case cannot be passed or failed as written, and the reason is the case, not the product.
Its expected result asks that “each row shows the COMPLETE telephone, with the bit you typed highlighted inside it”. But the word it tells you to type, ZZLONGROW, is part of a customer NAME and matches no telephone anywhere; and the written requirement this suite quotes puts the telephone on hover, not on the row. So neither half of the expected result can be reached with the data the case gives, and a pass or a fail would be invented.
What I saw anyway: three customers come back, and on all three the typed word is highlighted inside the full name. No telephone appears on any of them, and hovering does not bring one up.
What needs to happen: the expected result needs rewording by whoever owns it. I have not touched it.

146222.why:
What I did: the written requirement says a customer row shows four things — the name, the address, a count of open work orders, and the telephone when you hover over the row. I checked them on a customer that has all four on file: 7 Star Truck Repair, whose record carries the phone number 609-461-6502.
What I saw: three of the four are there — the name, “30 open”, and the address. The telephone never appears. Hovering over the row changes nothing at all.
How I know the hover worked: the row registers as hovered while the pointer is on it, and the same reading picks up the “30 open” marker beside it. So the row is being read correctly and the telephone is genuinely not shown.
One correction to my own first reading: I initially also reported the open-work-order count as missing. That was wrong — I was looking for it in the wrong place, and the customers I first tried simply had no open work orders to count. The count is present and correct.
